title: The Five Distance Theorem For An Arbitrary Norm
summary: The three gap theorem states that the points of the Kronecker sequence $α,2α,\ldots,Nα$, considered modulo one, divide the circle into intervals of at most three distinct lengths. In a two-dimensional nearest-neighbour analogue, Haynes and Marklof proved that the Kronecker sequence modulo an arbitrary unimodular lattice determines at most five distinct nearest-neighbour distances in the Euclidean norm, and that this bound is sharp. Dettmann subsequently constructed examples attaining five distinct distances for every $\ell_p$-norm, $1\leq p\leq\infty$. We prove the corresponding upper bound…
